div.l: And in adủersitee full abidyng and pacient
For whiche he was p̉erued often sithes
Full loth were hym to curs for his tithes
But rather wold he geven out of doute
Vn to his poure ꝑperisshyns aboute
Of his offryng and eke of his substance
He koude in litell thing haue suffisance
Wyde was his ꝑperissh and houses fer a sondre
But he left nought for reyne ne for thondre
In sekenes and in myschief to visite
The ferthest in his ꝑperissh moch and lite
Vp on his fete and in his hande a staffe
This noble ensaumple to his shepe he yaffe
That first he wrought and afterwarde taught
Out of þe gospell he tho wordes caught
And þis figure he added eke there to
That yf gold rust what shold Iren do
For yf a preste be foule on wham we truste
No wondre ys a lewde man to rust
And shame it is yf a prest take kepe
A sheten sheperd and a clene shepe
Wele aught a prest ensaumple for to yeve
By his clennes how þat his shepe shold leve
He set nought his benefice to hire
And lete his shepe accombred in the mire
Ne renne to londou to Seint Poules
To seche hym a chauntry for soules
Or be wᵗith a bretherhede wᵗithhold
But dwelled at home and kept wele his fold
So þat þe wolf made þ̉ere no maistrye
He was a shepard and not a m̉ersonarye
And though he holy were and v̉ertuous
He was nat wᵗith synfull men despitous
Ne of his speche daungerous ne digne
But in his speche discrete and benigne
To drawen folk to heven by feirenesse
By gode ensaumple þis was his besynesse
But and he knewe ony ꝑperson obsternate
Whether he were hiegh or lowe astate
Hym wold he snebbe for þe nones
